description: Emit a custom event for one subscriber, exactly as an integration or the public API would. This is the supported way to exercise event triggers, matching-field idempotency, branch conditions, and stop conditions end to end without waiting for real traffic. The event is recorded, sync rules apply, and matching event_received sequences enroll. Without automations:trigger the call succeeds but starts no sequence (sequenceTriggersRan false, reason missing_scope). Creates the subscriber if they do not exist. Use trigger_subscriber_events for several events on the same contact.

account.description: Organization (account) external ID or a reference object. Organizations are your customers' companies, not the Sequenzy account from get_account. Once the workspace has Organizations on, this creates the organization if missing, attaches this contact before the event, and supplies event.organization.* (and event.account.*) properties. Otherwise it is ignored and the result includes accountIgnored; create an account with upsert_account first. An object must contain externalId; role, name, domain and attributes are optional. Omit role to preserve existing membership roles.

externalId.description: Customer-owned organization ID. Required for an object reference.

attributes.description: Custom attributes to set on the subscriber.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

email.description: Subscriber email address. Provide email or externalId to identify the subscriber.

event.description: Event name, such as saas.purchase or invoice.paid. The event definition is created if it does not exist.

eventId.description: Your own id for this event, used as an idempotency key on both paths. For a live event, re-sending an id this contact already has for this event name writes nothing, runs no side effects, and returns the existing event with duplicate: true. For a historical event, the response remains historical: true and reports the skipped row in duplicates instead. Live deduplication is best-effort for calls sent within about a second of each other, so a producer that needs a strict guarantee should also keep its own ledger.

externalId.description: Customer-owned subscriber ID. Provide email or externalId to identify the subscriber.

firstName.description: First name applied to the subscriber profile.

lastName.description: Last name applied to the subscriber profile.

occurredAt.description: When the event actually happened (ISO 8601). Omit for live events. If this is more than an hour in the past the event is recorded as history: it is stored with its real timestamp and counts for segments and the timeline, but no sequences enroll, no sync rules apply, no waiting steps resume, and no webhooks fire. A historical event also moves the contact's signup date back to when it occurred (never later), so imported contacts do not read as added today. Use this when backfilling from another platform - never to fake a live event, since the side effects you are testing will not run.

properties.description: Event properties. Include the sequence's matching field (for example order.id or invoice.id) when testing idempotency or cancellation by field value.

name: trigger_subscriber_event

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `trigger_subscriber_event` MCP tool.

account.description: The account membership (externalId, role, created), when an account reference was provided record returned by Sequenzy.

accountIgnored.description: Present when `account` was ignored because the workspace has not turned Accounts on. Contains reason (accounts_not_enabled) and message.

duplicate.description: Present and true for a repeated live eventId. Nothing was written and no side effects ran; `event` is the existing event. Historical responses report skipped rows in `duplicates` instead.

duplicates.description: Historical event rows skipped because their idempotency receipt already existed.

event.description: The Live event with its name and whether the event definition was created. Historical responses use `events` instead. record returned by Sequenzy.

events.description: List of Historical events, each with id, name, and occurredAt. records returned by Sequenzy.

items.description: One item in the returned collection.

historical.description: Present and true when occurredAt selected the historical import path.

inserted.description: Historical event rows inserted by this request.

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: Human-readable status, confirmation, or next-step message.

sequenceTriggersRan.description: False when no sequence could start from this call (see sequenceTriggersSkippedReason).

sequenceTriggersSkippedReason.description: missing_scope: key lacks automations:trigger (write still applied). not_requested: enrollInSequences false. historical: recorded as history.

sideEffectFailures.description: Sync-rule or automation side effects that failed. The event itself is still recorded.

subscriber.description: The subscriber record returned by Sequenzy.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
